sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling with a randomized finite-support instrument conditional on each finite covariate stratum.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional multinomial cell probabilities are empirical within \((x,z)\); finite-sample inversion uses cellwise Clopper--Pearson intervals and asymptotics use their multinomial influence vectors.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper learns deterministic categorical rules by minimizing a loss formed from coordinatewise action-mean intervals and explicitly leaves randomized rules for future development.
Proposition 1 characterizes all minimax allocations when every action-specific spike state is feasible.
Theorems 2 and 3 establish local asymptotic minimaxity of an empirical-success statistical treatment rule with many point-identified treatments under an asymptotically balanced sampling design.

Theorem 5.1 gives a binary stochastic policy whose treatment probability is formed from lower and upper bounds on a conditional treatment-effect contrast and improves the deterministic worst-case-regret bound.
Theorem 1 gives necessary and sufficient inequalities for compatibility of a full categorical-instrument counterfactual distribution.
Response functions and linear programming deliver tight symbolic bounds for finite causal models.
Randomized minimax regret over a finite uncertainty set is representable as a zero-sum linear program.
Random-right-hand-side linear programs have optimizer limits whose form depends on degeneracy and the selection rule.
Auxiliary linear programs yield limits and confidence sets for optimal solutions when the constraint matrix and objective are fixed and the right-hand side is random.
Directionally differentiable maps require derivative-aware inference and generally invalidate the ordinary bootstrap when full differentiability fails.
Criterion inversion constructs confidence regions for parameter sets defined by population minimization.
Local Gaussian limit experiments characterize asymptotically minimax treatment rules when partially identified bounds shrink at the root-n scale.

body.tldr: For the binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1, the paper identifies the full joint action-mean polytope and solves the resulting randomized minimax-regret game.  The exact three-action witness has joint rule \(q^\dagger=(0,1/4,3/4)\) and value \(3/16\), whereas rectangularization selects \((0,0,1)\) with value \(1/4\); mixing its latent law with the uniform law on all 72 response types yields complete full-support observable laws that retain a regret-value gap of at least \(1/32\) and separated optimizer neighborhoods.  On separated nondegenerate unique faces, the moving-coefficient KKT map has a uniform root-\(n\) Gaussian law.  Internally, the model also contains a displayed codimension-one face intersection at which class-uniform honest contraction fails at every vanishing rate absent separation.  This is an existential model-limit result, not a characterization of every intersection or a refutation of any named method.  The exact Bonferroni Clopper--Pearson confidence-fiber union remains uniformly valid there, without a contraction claim.  Pure-rule certificates, the spike-state specialization, an operational rectangle-preservation certificate, and deployed-regret certification complete the supporting decision analysis.

project_justification.gap: Song et al.'s model M1 supplies response-law compatibility restrictions for discrete instruments and outcomes, but it does not provide randomized minimax-regret optimization or sampling inference for the resulting optimizer correspondence.  Existing random-linear-program theory generally fixes constraint normals, while here the observable multinomial table changes both feasible response bases and active regret coefficients.  The inferential issue is therefore twofold: derive regular laws on which the active KKT face is stable, and determine whether the maintained model itself contains face intersections that obstruct class-uniform honest contraction without separation.
project_justification.niche: The paper studies the binary-outcome, finite-covariate-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s M1 and links response-type partial identification to a finite randomized saddle program.  It separates a positive theory on laws satisfying explicit basis, rank, slack, reduced-cost, active-weight, and unique-face margins from an internal existential obstruction: a displayed admissible local submodel passes through a codimension-one optimal-face intersection and prevents class-uniform vanishing-rate contraction when such intersections are not excluded.
project_justification.fill: The positive result gives an explicit moving-coefficient derivative and a uniform Gaussian policy-and-value law on separated nondegenerate unique faces.  The negative result constructs one full-compliance local submodel inside the maintained class on which no data-based random closed set can combine the stated uniform asymptotic containment coverage with contraction at any vanishing rate; it neither classifies every face intersection nor refutes a named external workflow.  Exact finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage is the valid noncontracting fallback.  The three-action rectangle-safety witness is strengthened by a uniform-response-type perturbation with positive observed cells, treatment support, conditional outcome variance, a value gap of at least \(1/32\), and disjoint optimizer neighborhoods.  The simultaneous value-and-argmin rectangle certificate is retained as an operational supporting characterization, not claimed as theorem-level novelty.

body.related_work: Manski2000TreatmentChoice separates treatment choice from point identification, and Stoye2007ManyTreatments supplies the spike-state population allocation benchmark recovered here when every spike is feasible. Masten2023ManyTreatmentRules and MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Asymptotics analyze different repeated-sample or local-Gaussian treatment-choice problems, whereas this paper studies fixed-law inference for a population mixed-action optimizer under partial identification. Cui2021PartialIDDecisions randomizes a binary action from marginal contrast bounds; it does not optimize three or more actions against a joint categorical-instrument response polytope. SongEtAl2026CategoricalIV supplies model M1’s response-law compatibility restrictions; the present model is its binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization, not a claim about all of models M1--M5. SachsEtAl2023SymbolicBounds and MastinJailletChin2014RandomizedRegret provide the response-function linear-program and finite-saddle ingredients, whose composition is background. HruzaEtAl2026CategoricalPIL studies a broader overlapping bound-agnostic class and releases a multicategory implementation; the exact and full-support perturbed witnesses provide concrete regression targets for the coordinatewise-rectangle decision rule, while the paper’s positive response-basis and KKT theorem does not transfer by class inclusion. BonnansShapiro2000Perturbation informs the separated-face analysis. KlattMunkZemel2022RandomLP and LiuBuneaNilesWeed2023LPConfidence concern adjacent fixed-coefficient formulations, and FangSantos2019DirectionalInference motivates derivative-aware inference for nonsmooth maps. HiranoPorter2012Impossibility provides general impossibility results for nondifferentiable functionals; in contrast, the negative theorem here is the narrower model-specific construction of a categorical-IV local experiment with an exactly computed optimizer correspondence that changes across a codimension-one face tie. It neither subsumes Hirano--Porter’s theory nor claims to refute a named method. ClopperPearson1934Binomial and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007Sets inform the exact, noncontracting confidence-fiber fallback.
body.interpretation: The exact witness shows why the joint geometry of partially identified action means matters for treatment choice: the feasible inequality \(\mu_0\leq\mu_2\) changes both the optimal randomized policy and its worst-case regret relative to coordinatewise rectangularization.  The uniform-response-type perturbation shows that this failure persists on complete laws with positive observed cells, positive treatment support, and nondegenerate conditional outcomes; only a conservative \(1/32\) value-gap guarantee and disjoint optimizer neighborhoods are asserted away from the exact law.  For inference, separated unique faces admit ordinary root-\(n\) Gaussian analysis, while the displayed face intersection witnesses a class-uniform obstruction unless a separation condition is imposed.  At such irregular laws the confidence-fiber union is useful because validity, rather than contraction, is its guarantee.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The Gaussian policy-and-regret law is restricted to the observable nondegenerate unique-face class with fixed-support, response-basis, rank, slack, reduced-cost, and active-weight margins.  The face-intersection result is existential and internal to the maintained model: one displayed codimension-one local submodel rules out the specified class-uniform honest contraction at every vanishing rate absent separation.  It does not characterize all intersections and does not refute Hruza et al., Fang--Santos, or fixed-matrix linear-program procedures.  The Bonferroni confidence-fiber union remains valid but may be conservative and noncontracting.  The rectangle witness has a complete full-support perturbation with explicit positivity and variance margins, but for \(\delta>0\) only a gap of at least \(1/32\) and disjoint optimizer neighborhoods are guaranteed; the exact \(1/16\) gap and exact optimizer formulas are asserted only at \(\delta=0\).
body.honest_scope: The maintained causal model is the binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1, with finite randomized instrument support, categorical treatment, response-type exogeneity, consistency, exclusion, positive stratum--instrument support, and response-fiber compatibility.  The response-function projection and its composition with a finite randomized-regret linear program are background ingredients.  Uniform root-\(n\) Gaussian inference is proved only on the separated nondegenerate unique-face class.  Without separation, the model contains a particular full-compliance codimension-one face intersection at which the stated class-uniform honest contraction to the exact optimizer correspondence fails at every vanishing rate; no claim is made that every intersection has been classified or that a named external estimator or workflow is invalid.  The exact Bonferroni Clopper--Pearson confidence-fiber set remains finite-sample valid without a contraction claim.  The simultaneous rectangle value-and-argmin condition is an operational supporting certificate rather than a novelty claim.  The exact three-action rectangle counterexample is supplemented by full-support perturbations, but its exact optimizer identities and exact \(1/16\) gap are not claimed to persist after perturbation.
